brand.disclaimerLong: This game is a private fan project and not an official offering of BOKU University (University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna). No BOKU logos or photos are used; design and rooms are recreated. Prof. Haferkorn and all students are fictional. The subject matter has been carefully researched but is no substitute for an actual course.

help.title: Controls & rules
help.lead: You're sitting in the Animal Nutrition lecture, secretly playing tic-tac-toe. Prof. Haferkorn doesn't see everything – but more than you think.
help.v.laptop: Lean over the laptop or look back up
help.v.play: At the laptop: move the cursor and click a square (or press 1–9 on the numpad)
help.v.notes: Take notes – looks diligent and fills your notes for exam questions
help.v.alttab: Switch between game and lecture notes
help.v.lid: Close the lid further (less glow) or open it
help.v.sign: Sign the field-trip list when it reaches you (mouse gesture)
help.v.quiz: Answer an exam question · peek at your notes
help.v.touch: Swipe = view/cursor, tap = click, buttons at the bottom
help.rules:
• Attention: movement, glow and keeping your head down catch his eye – even from the corner of his eye.
  • Suspicion: when he looks on purpose, suspicion grows. Taking notes and correct answers reduce it.
  • Evidence: only from a direct look at your laptop with the game open. At 100 % you are caught.
  • People sitting in front of you hide you. Behind a broad back you're safer.
  • When the chalk stops scratching, he usually turns around – sometimes he only bluffs.
  • Caught three times: you're thrown out – or, if you were diligent, moved to the front row.
credits.title: Imprint, sources & licences
credits.body:
Tic Tac Tierernährung is a non-commercial fan project. It is not an official offering of BOKU University (University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna). All persons are fictional.

The subject matter (proximate analysis, van Soest fractions, energy and protein evaluation, rumen physiology, minerals, ration calculation) was compiled from textbooks and freely accessible sources; the source list is in docs/RECHERCHE.md.

The lecture hall, website and BOKUonline look are recreated; no BOKU logos or photos are used.
